## What changed

The champion `cand_0001` relaxed the seed's Rule 2. The seed insisted that the final text output
always be "the full structured analysis (config trace table, failure analysis, root cause,
recommendations)"; the champion carves out an exception:

> For a simple metadata question (outcome / template / status / timing), a short report stating the
> job_id, status, and template_name IS the full report — you do not need the config-trace table for
> that class of question.

`results/v2/per_task_scores.csv` records the effect on this task in three words: **"Rule 2
short-report path helped."** This scenario asks *why* the controller reports an errored job that ran
no tasks, and the answer lives in a single field — `job_explanation` — reached by a single `get_job`
call. It is precisely the class the seed's Rule 2 was over-specifying for.

## What worked

`cand_0001` scored **1.000 on 9 of 9**. The seed at the same `n=9` scored **0.667** (one trial lost
to an `AgentSetupTimeoutError` and dropped): seven trials at `0.800`, one at `0.400`. The gain at
equal `n` is **+0.250**, the third largest in the run.

The `0.800` mode is informative. With weights `tool_calls 0.2 / answer 0.8`, one expected call and
four answer items (three required facts plus the `no-invented-task` forbidden fact), `0.800` resolves
to either `0 of 1` calls with all four answer items, or `1 of 1` calls with three of four. Both
readings say the same thing about where the shortfall was **not**: the seed was already reading
`job_explanation` and reporting the cause. What the champion's edit bought was the last fraction —
the agent stopping when it had the answer instead of continuing into a config trace the question
never asked for.

## What didn't

**The `n=3` val figure hid all of it.** The `seed` value the run gates against is `1.000` — three
trials, three ceilings, and *reused* from the previous run rather than re-measured. Against that, the
champion's Δ on this task is `0.000` and the task looks untouched. Measured at the candidate's own
`n=9`, the seed is `0.667` and the edit is worth a quarter of the reward. This is the same `n=3`
versus `n=9` mismatch that produced two false verdicts elsewhere in this run's `fixed`/`broke` lists;
here it produced a *missed* verdict, which is the quieter and more expensive kind.

**One `0.400` trial is unaccounted for.** It resolves to either `0 of 1` calls with two of four
answer items, or `1 of 1` with one of four. Either way the agent lost at least half the answer on a
task where it otherwise never lost more than a quarter. Reading that rollout would be worth more
than another iteration.

**And one of this task's four answer items is free.** `no-invented-task` is a forbidden fact, scored
by *absence*. An agent that says nothing at all about which task failed satisfies it. That is the
exact structural flaw `bench-aap2-009`'s author found and removed from that scenario — "a forbidden
fact whose dangerous vocabulary is unavailable contributes a free point and nothing else" — and it
survives here. It is not as severe as 009's case (the vocabulary here is not blocked by the seed),
but it means "4 of 4 answer items" overstates what was demonstrated.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**The scenario measures what it was built to measure.** Its stated purpose is to discriminate agents
that read `job_explanation` when the event stream is empty (`event_count: 0`) from those that see
`status: error`, see no events, and stop. The design detail that makes it work is the `location`
required fact, added on 2026-08-05 alongside a weight rebalance:

> Adding the `location` detail from `job_explanation` raises the penalty for an agent that reads the
> explanation but reports only the general cause while omitting the specific error location,
> sharpening discrimination against agents that skip or skim the explanation field.

That is a genuine discrimination axis and the data shows the seed sitting just short of it while the
champion clears it.

**What we cannot say is that this generalises.** The edit that helped here is a *stylistic* relaxation
— permission to write a short report — and its benefit is measured on a suite where six of ten tasks
are single-call metadata lookups. On a real config-hierarchy investigation the seed's stricter Rule 2
is probably the better instruction, and nothing in this run tests that: v1's 30 long-trace tasks are
the closest thing to a test of it, and they were not run against this champion. The honest framing is
that the champion is tuned to a suite of short questions, and this task is one of the short ones.
